condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :Annual Work Plan | Description :(a) SID and PDMA Sindh will prepare draft annual work plan and budget for eachsubsequent year of Project implementation including all Project activities financed from the Credit as well as Counterpart Funds.(b) Safeguard Documents acceptable to the Bank required prior to the implementation of the activities included in the draft AnnualWork Plan and Budget have been prepared, or are in the process of being prepared. | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :Counterpart Funds | Description :The Project Implementing Entity shall provide counterpart funds with anequivalent amount to USD 20,000,000 for the financing of the Project. These funds shall be primarily allocated to the financing ofsalaries of the officials, operation and maintenance of infrastructure assets, acquisition of land, and cost of resettlement andother activities carried out to comply with the provisions of the Safeguard Documents. The allocation of Counterpart Funds shall bespecified in the Annual Work Plans and Budgets. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Procurement | Description :SID and PDMA Sindh shall establish within six months of Effectiveness and maintainthe system throughout Project implementation: (a) a system for the handling of procurement complaints acceptable to the Bank; and,(b) a procurement documentation and record keeping system acceptable to the Bank. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Recruitment for Project Implementing Agencies | Description :The Recipient shall cause the Government of Sindhto ensure that: (a) PDMA Sindh and SID shall provide and maintain officials and staff in sufficient numbers to implement theProject;(b) Staff working on the Project at SID and PDMA Sindh is selected or recruited on the basis of terms of reference,qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Bank; (c) full financial and administrative authority for the Project isdelegated to the Project Director at each Implementing Agency; and(d) the Director at each Implementing Agency is working fulltime as Director for the Project.In addition to the Implementing Agencies' current staff, the following resources will berecruited and maintained with terms of reference, qualification and experience acceptable to the Bank: (i) for PDMA Sindh: nolater than three (3) months after the Effective Date, a financial management specialist, and a dedicated procurement and contractadministration specialist; and(ii) for SID: no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, a financial managementspecialist, a dedicated procurement and contract administration specialist and an internal auditor. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Review of Performance | Description :The Bank and the Government of Sindh shall carry out joint reviews, interalia including: (a) an in-depth review of the Project within 12 months of Effectiveness, or such other period as may be agreed withthe Bank; and, (b) a midterm review of the Project by November 30, 2018, or any other date agreed with the Bank. The Government ofSindh will furnish regular progress reports to the Bank before each review.The Recipient will assess on a six monthly basis inconjunction with the Bank and Implementing Agencies: (i) the performances of the Director and other key management, fiduciary andtechnical staff members/consultants at Implementing Agencies; (ii) the timely carrying out of the respective contribution ofproject staff to the Annual Work Plans and Budgets; and (iii) progress of implementation of Project activities. | Frequency:CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Safeguards | Description :The Recipient and the Project Implementing Entity to ensure that the Project shall beimplemented in accordance with the guidelines, procedures, timetables and other specifications set forth in the SafeguardDocuments.Prior to the implementation of each infrastructure subproject, appropriate instruments - Environmental and Social ImpactAssessment (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), and/or Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) - should be preparedwhich is satisfactory to the Bank. In addition, all activities shall be consistent with the Recipient's own laws relating toenvironment and social safeguards. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

title.narrative: Length of embankments rehabilitated or constructed
Number of Risk identification studies completed

comment.narrative:
The number (30) reported in the last ISR reflected the number of districts in Sindh covered by the studies.
The 4 major studies completed are: 1. Sindh Hazards and Risk Atlas - covering the province and 29 districts 2. Sindh Informed Disaster Management Plan 3. Organizational Capacity Assessment and Development of Capacity Enhancement Plan. 4. Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM): Identification of Flood-Prone Districts.
Based on completed civil works including flood embankments and small recharge dams

title.narrative: Land area protected through project interventions from natural disasters, including:

comment.narrative: Based on the rehabilitation of 9 embankment sections and construction of 70 small recharge dams.

title.narrative: Number of small recharge dams constructed

comment.narrative: The project support the construction of small rainwater-fed recharge dams, less than 10 meters in height. The dams were constructed in the divisions of Hyderabad (32), Karachi (15), Mirpur Khas (18), Sukkur (3), and Shaheed Benazirabad (2).

title.narrative: Number of people at risk receiving timely and more accurate early warning notifications.

comment.narrative:
The target of 5 million people was established at the project's inception based on historical data of populations residing in high-risk flood-prone areas. The actual achievement was determined by tracking the number of individuals who received early warning notifications, based on data provided by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority
The dissemination approach was multi-faceted, targeting at-risk individuals identified through demographic data provided by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) and cellular providers via a third-party firm. The messaging system employed robocalls and Interactive Voice Response (IVR) for direct engagement, alongside SMS alerts for rapid mass communication. These tools were activated during multiple emergencies, including urban flooding, heatwaves, and the COVID-19 pandemic, ensuring timely delivery of critical information to vulnerable populations.

title.narrative: Development of SOPs for Sindh Disaster Management Fund (SDMF)

comment.narrative: This indicator is partially achieved. The amount allocated was diverted to respond to COVID-19.

actual.value: Draft SOPs developed for Sindh Disaster Management Fund.

title.narrative: Improved institutional capacity for disaster and climate risk management.

baseline.value: No SOPs for Sindh disaster fund; limited disaster management plans at sub-national levels.

target.value: Integrated disaster management plans adopted by government departments at sub-national levels.

comment.narrative:
This indicator is evaluated based on the benchmarks set in the PAD and revised during the project restructuring.
The revised results framework had the following deficiencies for this indicator: while the development of the disaster risk financing strategy was removed from the annual benchmark targets from the main section, operationalization of SOPs for the SDMF was not, even though at the stage of the Additional Financing and Restructuring it was already known this activity would not be achieved and respective funding was already repurposed for the COVID-19 support. However, in the M&E plan for the PDO indicators section of the Results Framework, both were still listed as part of the benchmarks for this indicator.

actual.value: Disaster Management Plans, informed by the multi-hazard risk assessment studies, were developed for and adopted by the Province and all 30 districts. Emergency Operation Center is fully operational at the PDMA Sindh. Improved flood risk information is available for planning.

title.narrative: Establishment of a Decision Support System (DSS) for SID

comment.narrative: SID has installed - gauging stations at the Guddu, Sukkur and Kotri barrages for real-time river flow data collection and transmission to the DSS to enable effective modelling. The DSS has increased real-time flood simulation capabilities and its integration into SID's operations for effective flood management and decision-making. During the 2022 floods, the DSS proved to be highly effective in assisting the GoS, in managing the crisis. The services provided by the DSS enabled all institutions involved in the flood response to make informed decisions.

title.narrative: Development and adoption of operational procedures for responding to disasters

comment.narrative: Indicator fully achieved. The Operational procedures are part of the Integrated disaster management plans which were adopted at eth provincial and district levels.

title.narrative: Percentage of labor force employed for small dam construction who are female

comment.narrative: Participation includes both construction and allied work. The indicator target was not achieved due to the overly ambitious target.

baseline.value: No dedicated capacity to respond to emergencies.

target.value: Specialized teams established in Karachi and Divisional Headquarters of Sindh to respond to disasters and emergencies, including public health emergencies.

comment.narrative: The SERS (Rescue 1122) made operational in six divisional HQs – Karachi, Larkana, Mirpurkhas, Sukkur, Hyderabad and Shaheed Benazirabad. Additional districts covered by ambulatory services. These are fully equipped and have trained staff.

actual.value: Specialized teams established in Karachi and Divisional Headquarters of Sindh to respond to disasters and emergencies including public health emergencies.

title.narrative: Establishment of a dedicated gender desk at emergency rescue service

comment.narrative: A dedicated gender desk at SERS HQ in Karachi provides a safe space to women to report gender-based violence, with calls handled confidentially by female officers who offer support, guidance, and referrals. However, availability of the female staff for the night shifts is a challenge.

title.narrative: Development of DMIS including Health Surveillance Dashboard

comment.narrative: DMIS dashboard incorporates modules which integrate the outcomes of the multi-hazard risk assessment, Sindh GIS, Disaster Warning and Information, Weather Forecast, Store Inventory and Relief Distribution, Rapid Damage Assessment, Rapid Response and Rescue Coordination; Vehicle Tracking, and Video Conferencing.

title.narrative: Percentage of first responders employed through the emergency rescue service which are female

comment.narrative:
The PDMA PIU informed about the discrepancies in the earlier reported achievements. Based on the data provided at the ICR stage, the share of female first responders employed through the emergency rescue service under the SRP is 1%: 5 females out of the total of 498 staff recruited, for SERS.
The share improved under SFERP–72 females out of the 704 staff recruited, or10.2%.
Overall, as of now, the female participation rate is around 6.4% - 77 females out of the 1,202 staff recruited, (SRP and SFERP).
